chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Yahya, brother of Darim, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
Bashfulness (al-hayā') and faith (al-īmān) are paired in one coupling; so when one of the two departs, its companion follows it.

key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: Bashfulness, modesty, or shyness in a spiritual and ethical context
key_terms.وَالْإِيمَانُ: And faith, belief in God and the divine message

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between bashfulness and faith in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that hayā' is not merely a social virtue but a fundamental component of īmān, often described as the 'garment' of the believer. The metaphor of them being 'tied in a knot' (maqarūn) signifies their mutual dependence, implying that the erosion of modesty inevitably leads to the decay of faith, a concept central to understanding the moral character of the Ahl al-Bayt.
